architecture.mechanism: Controlled charge/discharge of vehicle battery using local frequency measurements to stabilize electrical power and reduce voltage/frequency fluctuations during transients.
architecture.intervention: Install a voltage/frequency supervisory controller on the 2021 Subaru Outback that monitors the 12V bus and instrument panel supply; when it detects undervoltage or stall-correlated droop, it commands the high-voltage battery (or a DC-DC boost stage) to discharge into the 12V bus and momentarily assist the alternator/regulator to hold the instrument panel and ECU rails above the reset threshold.
architecture.expected_effect: Prevents instrument panel blackout and engine stall at idle and during transient electrical loads by actively stabilizing bus voltage, restoring sustained engine operation and electrical system function.
architecture.falsification_test: On a dynamometer, induce the stall condition (simulated alternator drop at idle with accessory load) and run 50 trials with the controller enabled vs. 50 disabled; the intervention is falsified if instrument panel dropout rate or engine stall rate does not drop by at least 80% with the controller active, or if post-repair stall events recur in normal driving within 500 miles.

challenge.kill_reason: the mechanism-space distinctness adjudication counts 1 materially distinct mechanism(s) (< 2, mechanism_distinctness/2.0.0) — the run generated nothing worth attacking (Art. LXXXIV, R514)
